descriptors.R: nominee of the party that held the presidency from 1969 to 1977
descriptors.D: nominee of the party of the administration in office since 1977, which also holds majorities in both houses of Congress
descriptors.O: independent candidate: a Midwestern congressman who left the primaries of the party out of power to run on fiscally conservative, socially liberal positions

slice_sources.men: 1980 census (April) carried to November 1980 along the 1970→1980 trend; men who are citizens 18+ (Twenty-sixth Amendment) outside the eleven Southern states: white non-Hispanic US-born, naturalized citizens of any race, Black US-born, and US-born Hispanic, Asian, Native American and other; 50 states and DC; calibrated to certified 1980 returns.
slice_sources.women: 1980 census (April) carried to November 1980 along the 1970→1980 trend; women who are citizens 18+ (Twenty-sixth Amendment) outside the eleven Southern states: white non-Hispanic US-born, naturalized citizens of any race, Black US-born, and US-born Hispanic, Asian, Native American and other; 50 states and DC; calibrated to certified 1980 returns.
slice_sources.south-white: 1980 census (April) carried to November 1980 along the 1970→1980 trend; citizens 18+ in the eleven former Confederate states other than Black US-born (white non-Hispanic US-born, naturalized of any race, and US-born Hispanic, Asian, Native American and other); calibrated to certified 1980 returns.
slice_sources.black-south: 1980 census (April) carried to November 1980 along the 1970→1980 trend; Black US-born citizens 18+ in the eleven former Confederate states; Voting Rights Act coverage continues. Any shortfall against white turnout is counted as exclusion.
slice_sources.immigrants: 1980 census (April) carried to November 1980 along the 1970→1980 trend; noncitizen adults of any race, who could not vote in any state.
